abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a revolutionary mechanism design framework that fundamentally transforms incentive compatibility in peer-to-peer networks, addressing the persistent free-riding problem through a paradigm shift in how cooperation emerges in decentralized systems. Traditional approaches rely on reputation systems or centralized verification, creating scalability bottlenecks and single points of failure that undermine the core principles of P2P computing. We propose a coalitional game-theoretic model where altruistic behavior emerges organically from a Shapley value-based reward mechanism that is provably immune to strategic manipulation. Our framework establishes that rational peers maximize individual utility while simultaneously optimizing collective welfare, a counterintuitive result that challenges conventional wisdom in P2P security research. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that the mechanism achieves core stability under realistic network conditions while maintaining communication complexity that scales logarithmically with peer population. Furthermore, we prove that the system satisfies strategy-proofness without requiring identity verification, thereby preserving anonymity while ensuring truthful contribution behavior. Extensive analytical evaluation across diverse network topologies confirms that this paradigm achieves near-optimal resource utilization while maintaining temporal fairness among participants. This work opens new research directions in decentralized incentive design and provides theoretical foundations for next-generation P2P protocols that eliminate free-riding without centralized intervention.

This paper presents a rigorous theoretical analysis that significantly advances our understanding of distributed hash table performance under realistic churn conditions, developing novel analytical models that substantially improve existing bounds for lookup operations in overlay networks. Prior analytical work has relied on simplifying assumptions regarding peer departure patterns that fail to capture the temporal correlations and burstiness inherent in real-world P2P networks. We develop a sophisticated stochastic process model that incorporates correlated failure events and derives tight bounds on lookup latency as an explicit function of network size, churn rate, and lookup timeout parameters. Our analysis reveals that the expected number of hops required for successful DHT lookups can be reduced by up to 40% compared to conventional Chord-based approaches through optimal bucket maintenance strategies. We further establish that the proposed adaptive refresh mechanism achieves near-optimal consistency while reducing message overhead by approximately 35% relative to naive stabilization protocols. The theoretical results provide actionable insights for designing more robust distributed hash tables that maintain efficient operation under severe churn conditions, contributing to the advancement of decentralized storage systems. These findings have direct implications for the design of production DHT implementations in content distribution networks.

We introduce a groundbreaking architecture that fundamentally reimagines the integration of blockchain technology with peer-to-peer content distribution networks, creating a new paradigm where consensus mechanisms and content delivery coexist as equals within a unified decentralized system. Existing hybrid approaches merely augment traditional P2P protocols with blockchain verification layers, introducing artificial boundaries that create translation overhead and architectural complexity. Our proposed system eliminates these limitations by treating blockchain state and P2P content as interdependent resources within a single overlay network, enabling novel applications where content addressing and state consensus influence each other in real-time. The architecture implements a hierarchical consensus mechanism where lightweight transactions for content metadata achieve millisecond confirmation while critical state changes leverage full distributed consensus with stronger finality guarantees. The system design incorporates novel peer discovery protocols that leverage both DHT-based lookups and blockchain state for hybrid routing decisions, significantly improving fault tolerance against both network partitions and adversarial participants. Implementation results demonstrate that this architectural paradigm achieves content distribution performance comparable to traditional CDN infrastructure while providing cryptographic content verification through the integrated blockchain layer, with the system supporting throughput exceeding 10,000 content-addressable operations per second.

We present StreamAdapt, a practical peer-to-peer streaming system that substantially enhances quality of service for live broadcasting scenarios through intelligent peer selection and adaptive bitrate mechanisms that significantly outperform existing mesh-based approaches. Prior P2P streaming systems suffer from suboptimal peer selection algorithms that fail to account for temporal variations in peer availability and bandwidth capacity, resulting in excessive buffering and poor playback quality during peak demand periods. StreamAdapt employs predictive machine learning models trained on historical peer behavior patterns to forecast availability and dynamically adjust the overlay topology for optimal streaming performance. The system incorporates novel forwarding strategies that balance bandwidth efficiency against playback continuity through real-time adaptation to network conditions. We design a distributed credit mechanism that incentivizes peers contributing upload bandwidth while preventing strategic bandwidth reservation that degrades overall system efficiency. Evaluation across diverse network conditions spanning thousands of concurrent viewers demonstrates that StreamAdapt achieves a 45% reduction in rebuffering events and 30% improvement in average video quality compared to state-of-the-art mesh-based P2P streaming protocols. The system maintains these performance gains while preserving computational efficiency suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices.
